source: Reference criterion: the epidemiology base population is already BMI >= 30 by the WHO NCD_BMI_30A definition, so this is a no-op multiplier (factor 1.0) included for a complete, auditable criterion stack.

Derived from CDC/NCHS NHANES obesity class distribution: severe obesity (BMI >= 40) is 9.7% of US adults against overall obesity of 40.3% (NCHS Data Brief 508, https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/products/databriefs/db508.htm); combined class II+III (BMI >= 35) is commonly estimated at roughly 45-50% of all obese adults from published NHANES class breakdowns. Approximation, not a single-figure citation.

General estimate for established CVD prevalence among adults with obesity, informed by the co-prevalence literature for cardiometabolic conditions (e.g. 20.9% co-prevalence of CVD and obesity among type 2 diabetes patients in a German claims study, Hennies et al. 2024, https://dom-pubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/dom.15931, used as a cross-reference point rather than an obesity-only observation).

General demographic estimate: adults aged 75+ are approximately 10-15% of the 18+ population in a mixed high- and middle-income market set (UN World Population Prospects age structure), so the 18-75 share is roughly 0.85-0.92. Not curated per market.

Modelling assumption: current anti-obesity GLP-1 treatment penetration remains low (around 2-8% of eligible adults per 2015-2023 US prescribing data), implying most of the addressable population is still treatment-naive. Not from a single cited study.

Modelling assumption: roughly half of treated type 2 diabetes patients remain above the ADA glycaemic target of HbA1c < 7%, consistent with commonly reported US/OECD glycaemic-control statistics. Not from a single cited study; global default pending per-country curation.

German claims data study (Hennies et al. 2024, Diabetes Obes Metab): 53.0% of type 2 diabetes patients had established cardiovascular disease. Low bound reflects a lower estimate from a Chinese multicentre cohort (14.9%, 3B study database) illustrating substantial geographic variation; high bound is the German figure. https://dom-pubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/dom.15931
